trigger: Breach of security: unauthorized access of electronic personal information (a name with a Social Security, passport, or financial account number, or geolocation, among other elements) of individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 additional days only if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected individual in Florida, by mail or email; the notice must give the date or date range, the information involved, and a farm contact. The farm sends worker notices in English and Spanish
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - current and former employees and H-2A workers whose files are in the Office folder (about 25 people)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination (the 15-day extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to the notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs, with a synopsis, the number affected, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: No at current scale - the farm holds personal information on about 25 people. Recheck if that changes

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the farm reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept for at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel decides. Farm policy: not relied on when Social Security, passport, or bank account numbers were taken with names

obligation: Law enforcement delay of individual notice
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation and asks in writing
deadline: Delay for the period stated in the written request
notify: Hold notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the farm (inbound)
trigger: A breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent (payroll service; H-2A filing agent)
deadline: Agent must notify the farm as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after its determination; the farm then gives the notices above
notify: The farm (Security Coordinator to be registered as breach contact, POAM-010)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track with the payroll service and the H-2A filing agent

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected former workers who now live outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law. H-2A workers at home-country addresses are notified by farm policy in Spanish
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of every affected person

obligation: H-2A earnings statements and records during an outage (continuity duty, not a notice)
trigger: Payroll, SYS-01 hours, or the Office folder unavailable during the incident
deadline: Earnings statement on or before each payday; records available within 72 hours of a DOL request when kept at a central office
notify: Each H-2A worker (statement); Department of Labor (on request)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 2 H-2A workers from February to July

obligation: Produce Safety records on FDA request during an outage (continuity duty, not a notice)
trigger: FDA requests records while SYS-01 or the office is unavailable
deadline: Readily available; 24 hours for records kept offsite

trigger: Determination that an article of food is a reportable food
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 24 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No for the farm - the duty is on a responsible party, the person who registers a food facility (350f(a)(1)); the farm registers none. If fertigation tampering may have affected harvested watermelons, tell the packer-shipper at once so it can assess its own duty

obligation: Packer-shipper notice of events affecting food safety, traceability, or loads
trigger: Any event that could affect product safety, lot traceability, or committed loads
deadline: Within 24 hours of the farm becoming aware (contract term)
notify: Packer-shipper field buyer and food safety contact

deadline: Per policy: call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring any vendor

obligation: MSP incident notice to the farm (inbound)
trigger: Security incident in the MSP's own systems or tools that could affect the farm
deadline: No term today; a 24-hour term is being added (P01 R-021)

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: FBI (IC3 or field office); CISA reporting
deadline: As soon as practical (Day 0-2 in the runbook)
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary; supports investigation and is an OFAC mitigating factor

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, food and agriculture entities are covered only above the SBA size standard (the farm is below it). Recheck when final

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the farm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
